name: John Quincy Adams
role: US secretary of state (1817–1825), president (1825–1829), and representative (1831–1848)
summary: Adams grounded government in the Declaration's natural rights and the sovereignty of the people, defended the Union against nullification and secession, and favoured federal improvements and a moderately protective tariff. He opposed slavery as inconsistent with the Declaration and valued civil and religious liberty, neutrality abroad and a civilian-led army.
